questions.question: Which statements about LangChain tools are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A tool gives an LLM a defined capability it can invoke
Tools can wrap APIs, functions, databases, or other external capabilities
Tools are only used for generating text
An agent can decide when to call a tool based on the task

questions.explanation: LangChain tools provide callable capabilities to AI applications. They can interact with APIs, databases, functions, and other systems. Agents can reason about when a tool is needed and invoke it.

questions.question: Which statements correctly describe the difference between a chain and an agent? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A chain generally follows a predefined execution flow
An agent can dynamically decide which tools or actions to use
A chain always requires an LLM
Agents are useful when the required sequence of actions is not completely predetermined

questions.explanation: Chains typically execute a known sequence of operations, while agents can dynamically choose actions and tools based on the task. A chain does not necessarily require an LLM.

questions.question: Which statements about cosine similarity between embedding vectors are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It measures the angle between two vectors
A value closer to 1 generally indicates greater directional similarity
It requires vectors to have exactly two dimensions
It is commonly used to compare semantic embeddings

questions.explanation: Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors and is commonly used with embeddings. Vectors pointing in similar directions have cosine similarity closer to 1, regardless of their dimensionality.
